correctness.rationale: For an \(r\)-dimensional message subspace \(U\), zero coordinates are exactly characteristic face vectors lying in \(U^\perp\), so the problem is to maximize the number of face vectors in a \((k-r)\)-subspace. Every \(s\)-subspace has an \(s\)-coordinate information set \(T\) on which projection is injective. Projection sends \(\chi_\sigma\) to \(\chi_{\sigma\cap T}\), which remains a face by downward closure, giving the sharp bound \(|D^*\cap L|\le|\Delta|_T|-1\). The coordinate subspace on \(T\) attains equality. This proves the universal formula. Exhaustive replay over all full-vertex complexes through four vertices over \(\mathbb F_2\) and \(\mathbb F_3\), direct enumeration of source Example 4.2, and finite cone-over-skeleton instances all agree with the formula.

originality.rationale: The 2026 primary source proves only the first generalized weight through its minimum-distance formula and gives no higher-weight theorem. The strongest prior paper devoted specifically to weight hierarchies from simplicial complexes gives a general intersection setup but evaluates only restricted maximal-face configurations and states that the general problem is difficult. For q=2 its defining set coincides with the present characteristic-face set, so the new projection formula resolves the arbitrary-complex binary case in one step. Exact-source, induced-subcomplex, hierarchy, and equivalent projection searches found no prior statement of the formula.
residual_risks: An older combinatorics or matroid source may contain the same information-set projection lemma under different terminology.
The theorem intentionally does not claim to solve the distinct q>2 vector-downset simplicial-complex construction.
The hierarchy of the source's specific finite examples may have been computed privately or in an unindexed database even though no published universal formula was found.

value.rationale: The result converts the 2026 source's minimum-distance theory into a complete generalized-weight theorem for every simplicial complex, with an especially simple induced-subcomplex invariant. It simultaneously extends field-independence from d1 to the full hierarchy, resolves the arbitrary-complex binary case left difficult in the dedicated 2025 hierarchy paper, and gives the full hierarchy of an infinite distance-optimal family from the recent source. These are structural consequences useful across the whole construction, not a routine finite computation.
